key_insight: XCAPE combines powder X-ray diffraction constraints with physics-guided structure search and a universal machine-learning interatomic potential to identify plausible crystal structures.
engineering_relevance: The framework can help convert experimental diffraction data into atomistic models for materials characterization and automated discovery workflows.
method: Constrain a symmetry-aware evolutionary search using composition, unit cell, space group, and PXRD data.
Explore Wyckoff-site configurations with tailored mutations and evaluate energy stability and diffraction agreement.
Accelerate geometry optimization with a universal machine-learning interatomic potential.
evidence_signal: XCAPE recovered 71/77 simulated-pattern benchmarks and all 12 experimental reference structures; among 12 additional candidate assignments without matching ICSD entries, 10 were within 10 meV/atom of the DFT convex hull.
watch_item: PXRD agreement and low predicted energy do not establish a unique structure, so new candidate assignments require independent experimental validation.
paper_title: Physics-Guided Crystal Structure Elucidation from Powder X-Ray Diffraction with Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
